meta.author: OpenMedia
meta.summary: Hides Guardian's sticky support banner, one-tap prompt, ads and looping videos; blur or hide card pictures
meta.notes:
Checked 2026-11-13, logged out, real Chrome (headless) on the Guardian international front page (theguardian.com/international) with iPhone UA 390x844 and desktop UA, DOM captured after 7 seconds. Fixtures `real.html` and `desktop-real.html` are sanitised excerpts (text and links stripped, needed ancestors only, `data-keep` on #maincontent and the header).

LIVE (same on both captures unless stated): `.ad-slot-container` 21, `.top-fronts-banner-ad-container` 9, `gu-island[name="StickyBottomBanner"]` 1, `gu-island[name="EditionSwitcherBanner"]` 1, `gu-island[name="GoogleOneTap"]` 1, `[data-component="gu-video-loop"]` 6, `picture img` 112, the newsletters, take-part and secure-messaging components 1 each, `[data-component="most-popular"]` 2, `[data-component="trending-topics"]` 1, `gu-island[name="CardCommentCount"]` 8. The original cookie, ad and app-banner rules matched nothing on this page (the Guardian's consent dialog lives in an iframe that the capture did not open).

Choices: Card pictures Show/Blur/Hide.

SOURCE: the Guardian list in jakubvalenta/adblock-lists hides `[name="EditionSwitcherBanner"]`; uBlock issue 7377 documents the big yellow contributions banner. Hooks are `gu-island` custom-element names and `data-component` values (Guardian's own stable analytics names); no hashed `dcr-*` classes are used.

NOT verified: article pages (the epic in the article body, the sign-in gate, related-content rails, comments), the live consent dialog, and sections other than the international front. Hiding the sticky banner does not stop the Guardian from showing in-article reader-revenue epics.
